subject: Climate & Environment
title: Who Runs Out of Water
description: Learn Who Runs Out of Water in one minute.

hook.text: About 2 billion people live in countries facing high water stress right now.

buildup.text: Water stress means demand is approaching or exceeding the available supply.

discovery.text: The Middle East and North Africa use over 80% of available freshwater every year.

twist.text: By 2025, half the world's population could be living in water-stressed areas.

climax.text: Water scarcity is not always about rainfall — it is often about mismanagement and waste.

punchline.text: Running out of water is not a future problem. It's a current one.

quiz.question: How many people currently live in water-stressed countries?

details.summary: About 2.3 billion people live in water-stressed countries, and projections suggest half the world's population could face water scarcity by 2050. The Middle East, North Africa, South Asia, and parts of sub-Saharan Africa are most vulnerable due to low rainfall, high demand, and poor infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: Water scarcity is not just a distant threat. It already limits economic growth, food production, and health in dozens of countries, and climate change is making it worse.
takeaways: About 2.3 billion people live in water-stressed nations
Half the world may face water scarcity by 2050
The Middle East and North Africa are most vulnerable

faq.question: What is the difference between water stress and water scarcity?
faq.answer: Water stress occurs when annual water supply drops below 1,700 cubic meters per person. Water scarcity is below 1,000 cubic meters, and absolute scarcity is below 500. These thresholds capture how supply relates to population and demand in a given area.

faq.question: Can technology solve water scarcity?
faq.answer: Technology like desalination, drip irrigation, and water recycling can help but is not a complete solution. Distribution equity, governance, conservation behavior, and addressing the root causes of overuse are all essential alongside technological advances.
